editorial:
The Wishing Ring: An Idyll of Old England is a silent comedy-drama released November 9, 1914 by World Film Manufacturing Company as a Shubert Feature. Maurice Tourneur directed it. Vivian Martin plays Sally, the parson's daughter, Alec B. Francis the Earl of Bateson and Chester Barnett his son Giles. Silent Era's cast list also includes Johnny Hines as a happy boy and Gyp Williams, whom it lists as a dog. The Internet Archive metadata lists Gyp Williams in the cast without describing it. A creator gets a Tourneur feature that survives, with a print in the Library of Congress film archive.

The film print is public domain in the US. It was published in 1914, and works first published in the US before 1931 are public domain due to copyright expiration (Cornell chart of US copyright terms). No renewal search was needed. Other layers are not cleared. The film adapts Owen Davis's play, and I could not confirm that play's publication or registration history, so check it before relying on the story. Any music on a modern copy is a separate work, and a copy made from the 35mm negative or another restoration may carry added material. Use the images with your own score or one you have cleared.
faq: Can I reuse the 1914 film footage of The Wishing Ring in the US?

Yes for the film print. It was published in 1914, and works first published in the US before 1931 are public domain due to copyright expiration (Cornell chart of US copyright terms). Check separately for any added score, titles or other new material in the copy you use.
Is the story free to adapt too?
Not confirmed. The film is based on Owen Davis's play, and I could not verify that play's publication or registration history. Check it before making a new adaptation of the story itself.
